sources.title: Great Lakes Water Protection Treaty
sources.author: Council of the Great Lakes
sources.excerpt: The Great Lakes, holding 20% of Earth's fresh water, are declared a protected commons.
sources.longExcerpt: By unanimous agreement of Indigenous nations, Canadian provinces, and American states, the Great Lakes are declared humanity's common heritage. No water shall be diverted beyond the watershed. No corporation may claim ownership. The lakes are healing: sturgeon return to ancestral spawning grounds, wild rice grows again in the shallows. Detroit and Toronto are reborn as water cities, their buildings filtering rain, their streets permeable. We are learning what the Anishinaabe always knew: water is life.
